newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps gain as gasoline leads market up.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps gain as gasoline leads market up.

text.p: European oil swaps bounced higher on Wednesday as gasoline futures led the market higher and crude found some support from bullish API data.

But news late on Tuesday that Iraq may only be allowed to carry over five percent of its $1 billion quarterly limit for oil sales into the second 90 day period of the oil-for-food deal with the United Nations cast a bearish shadow, some dealers said.

Delays to the resumption of oil sales under the second term of the agreement suggest Iraq will have to sell up to 1.5 million barrels per day in August compared with the previous quarter when 660,000 bpd were pumped in order to achieve the billion dollar target.
However, in the immediate term bouyant gasoline was taking centre stage and pulling the rest of the market in its wake.
Brent crude CFDs were a few cents firmer with July 21-25 pegged at -14/15 cents against September from -16 cents and July 28-August 1 went to -16 from -21 cents.
August 4-8 firmed to -20 cents against September from -22 cents as did August 11-15.
Gasoline hogged the limelight on paper as much as on futures. Dealers said August was pegged at $188.50, up $1 or so while September firmed to $187.50, up about $1.50-2.00.
Possible physical abitrage to the U.S. added a bullish tinge to the market.
Naphtha took comfort from firmer gasoline and rose about $1 a tonne with August pegged at $185-186 and less-talked July at $182.50-$184. Dealers said Asian demand was helping Europe edge higher.

Fuel oil gained about $1 or so with several deals done both prompt and further out around 1Q98. Dealers said July was around $87.75, August at $88.25 and September $89.25. A couple of July swaps traded at $87.50 and Q1 went at $95.
Low sulphur swaps were 50 cents or so stronger, but a good deal quieter than high sulphur. Q1 was talked around $103 and Aguust around $94.
Gas oil crack spreds were seen at $4.25 for 4Q97, $4.40 on 1Q98 and $4.05 on 2Q98.
